corrections.text: The article states that 'the effect was strongest specifically when the pump laser's photon energy matched the bandgap at the Γ point of the crystal, ruling out a simpler laser-assisted photoemission artifact, according to the Nature Physics paper.' The Nature Physics source (nature.com/articles/s41567-026-03341-0) is paywalled and could not be accessed directly by our editorial crawler or by manual verification attempts, including via the DOI resolver. The paper's arXiv preprint (arXiv:2502.11967) confirms the study's central finding — 'the first direct experimental observation of a Floquet topological state' driven by light-induced band inversion in SnTe — but its abstract does not include this level of methodological detail. This specific claim about Γ-point photon-energy matching and ruling out a photoemission artifact is scientifically plausible and consistent with standard pump-probe ARPES methodology, but it could not be independently verified against any source accessible to the editor at time of review.
